title: BBQ Smoker Temperature Stall Detection
dataSources: Sourdough monitor (`sourdough:reading`), BBQ/sous-vide probes (`bbq:probe`), fridge/freezer/oven temperature (`kitchen:appliance`), espresso shots (`espresso:shot`), pantry inventory (`pantry:item`), kombucha brew (`kombucha:reading`).
app: ESP32/ESPHome kitchen sensors (sourdough rise, BBQ/sous-vide probes, fridge/freezer temperature), espresso-shot logs, and pantry inventory via MQTT and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=bbq:probe probe=meat
| timechart span=10m avg(temp_c) as meat_temp
| streamstats current=f last(meat_temp) as prev
| eval climb=meat_temp-prev, stalled=if(climb<0.3 AND meat_temp>63 AND meat_temp<74,1,0)
description: Detects the notorious brisket stall, when the meat temperature plateaus for hours, so you know whether to wait it out or wrap.
value: The stall panics first-time smokers into ruining dinner; spotting it for what it is turns a scary plateau into a planned step.
implementation: Feed a meat-probe into `index=personal`; run during a cook and flag when the temperature climb flattens in the stall zone.
visualization: Line chart of meat temperature with the stall zone shaded.
grandmaExplanation: It spots when the meat's temperature stops rising for a while during a long cook, which is normal and just means keep going or wrap it.
